steps.title: Measure the cost of one sweep
steps.explanation: Both solvers use the same 48 linear tetrahedra, loads, masses, material and one 0.5 ms implicit step. The teal PCG solve supplies a checked residual reference for the orange compliant iteration.
steps.observe: One sweep visits 288 strain constraints. The orange residual is about 0.0438889 N and the maximum nodal difference is 4.73687 µm; display displacements are magnified 20 times.

steps.title: Spend five times the constraint work
steps.explanation: Change only the number of compliant sweeps. Keeping the physical problem fixed makes the numerical difference interpretable as finite-iteration error.
steps.observe: After 1440 constraint visits, residual falls to about 0.000504610 N and maximum nodal difference to 0.0781643 µm. The relative objective-norm error is about 0.00103718.

steps.title: Inspect agreement with the reference
steps.explanation: Increase to 20 sweeps and compare actual residuals. The algorithmic count alone does not prove convergence, time-step independence or agreement on a different model.
steps.observe: The compliant residual is about 2.90e-11 N for 5760 visits, close to the reference target 4.16e-11 N. This fixture supports the displayed comparison, not a general one-sweep accuracy claim.

audit.finding: Residual-only output did not expose the approximation error or constraint work, making a speed/accuracy comparison incomplete.
audit.change: Report nodal and objective-norm differences plus visits across one, five and twenty sweeps of one fixed problem.
audit.remaining: No wall-clock performance claim, collision-budget comparison, multigrid, reduced basis or general nonlinear XPBD qualification. Chapter implementation exercises remain explicitly unfinished.
